definition_zh: 抓住；夺取；扣押；突然发作
definition_en: to take hold of something quickly and firmly, often by force
core_image: 一只手猛地钳住猎物，毫不松开
scene: 海关检查到可疑包裹，执法人员立刻行动。 Customs officers seized the illegal goods at the harbor.
sceneCN: 这里 seize 是「扣押；没收」（第 3 个义项：依法强制占有）；句意是海关人员在港口查扣了违禁品。

derivatives.zh: seize 加 -ure 名词后缀，义为「 seizure 抓取；没收；癫痫发作」
seize 加 -er 名词后缀，义为「夺取者；抓捕者」

senses.title: To grab quickly and firmly
senses.definition: to take hold of something suddenly with force
senses.definitionCN: 突然用力抓住某物
senses.example: The policeman seized the thief's arm.
senses.exampleCN: 警察一把抓住小偷的手臂。
senses.why: The claw closes in one snap and nothing escapes.
senses.whyCN: 爪子瞬间合拢，猎物无处可逃。

senses.title: To take by force or power
senses.definition: to take control of a place or position using force
senses.definitionCN: 用武力或权力占据某地或某职位
senses.example: The army seized the capital in one night.
senses.exampleCN: 军队一夜之间攻占了首都。
senses.why: The claw becomes an army: whole cities snap shut in one grip.
senses.whyCN: 爪子变成军队：整座城市被一握合拢。

senses.title: To confiscate legally
senses.definition: to take property officially under the law
senses.definitionCN: 依法正式收走财物
senses.example: Police seized three cars in the fraud case.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在该诈骗案中扣押了三辆车。
senses.why: The state's hand closes around property, the legal version of the grip.
senses.whyCN: 国家的手合拢于财产之上——这就是抓握的法律版本。

senses.title: To grip the mind or body suddenly
senses.definition: to take hold of a person's mind or body at once
senses.definitionCN: 突然攫住人的心神或身体
senses.example: She was seized by a sudden cough.
senses.exampleCN: 她突然剧烈咳嗽起来。
senses.why: An invisible claw snaps around the chest or the nerves.
senses.whyCN: 一只看不见的爪子骤然合拢于胸口或神经。

senses.title: To use a chance eagerly
senses.definition: to take an opportunity immediately and eagerly
senses.definitionCN: 立即且热切地抓住机会
senses.example: He seized every chance to speak English.
senses.exampleCN: 他抓住一切机会说英语。
senses.why: The claw closes on time itself — the moment becomes the prey.
senses.whyCN: 爪子合拢于时间——那一刻成了猎物。

intro.en: From Old French saisir, which came from a Germanic word meaning to take possession.
intro.cn: 来自古法语 saisir，其源头是日耳曼语中表「占有」的词。

items.en: The likely source is a Germanic root meaning to take hold or sit upon, also linked to seat.
items.cn: 可能源自日耳曼词根，意为「抓住、坐据」，与 seat 有亲缘关联。

items.en: Old French saisir meant to take possession, especially of feudal property.
items.cn: 古法语 saisir 意为占有，尤指取得封建地产。

items.en: English law borrowed the word for taking property by legal authority.
items.cn: 英格兰法律借用该词表示依法占有财产。

items.en: Seize entered English in the 1400s with both grabbing and legal senses.
items.cn: 十五世纪 seize 进入英语，兼有抓取与法律占取二义。

items.en: Modern use adds seizing power, moments, emotions, and medical fits.
items.cn: 现代用法扩展到夺取政权、把握时机、情绪袭扰与医学发作。

note.en: Look-alikes in the sei- spelling family, and near rivals in the grabbing field.
note.cn: sei- 拼写家族的形近词，以及抓取义场的近义词。

entries.definition: how big something is
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸——与 seize 仅差词尾，且 seize 中的 ei 不发长音时易混淆

entries.definition: to stop
entries.definitionCN: 停止——形近音近但词源不同，来自拉丁 cessare

entries.definition: a military encirclement
entries.definitionCN: 围攻——与 seize 同出一脉，均为「占取」的军事化表达

entries.definition: to take hold suddenly
entries.definitionCN: 猛抓——口语色彩更强，seize 更正式

entries.definition: to hold firmly or understand
entries.definitionCN: 抓紧；理解——兼有比喻理解义

entries.definition: to officially take property
entries.definitionCN: 没收——与扣押义项近义，更书面

normalIntro.en: Hooks on the snapping claw and the siege connection.
normalIntro.cn: 基于猛合的爪子与 siege 关联的记忆钩子。

normal.en: siege and seize share one root: to take possession
normal.cn: siege 与 seize 同根，都表示「占有」

normal.en: size and seize differ by one letter and one vowel sound
normal.cn: size 与 seize 只差一个字母与一个元音

normal.en: seize the day means grab the moment with both hands
normal.cn: seize the day 就是双手抓住当下

normal.en: a seizure of assets is the legal claw
normal.cn: 扣押资产就是法律之爪

normal.en: be seized by fear: an emotion with teeth
normal.cn: be seized by fear：长着牙齿的情绪

abstract.en: Picture a falcon closing its talons in mid-air
abstract.cn: 想象猎鹰在空中猛然合拢利爪

abstract.en: See a gate slamming shut on a whole city
abstract.cn: 看见城门轰然合拢，围住整座城

abstract.en: Feel panic wrapping around your chest in one grip
abstract.cn: 体会恐慌一把攫住胸口的感觉

examples.en: The rebel leader seized the radio station first.
examples.cn: 叛军首领首先夺取了广播电台。

examples.en: Officers seized a shipment of fake medicine.
examples.cn: 官员们查扣了一批假药。

examples.en: A sudden panic seized the whole crowd.
examples.cn: 一阵恐慌突然笼罩了人群。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西子」——西子湖畔一把抓住，抓西湖美女的手可要又快又稳。

root: 古法语 saisir「占有」，源自法兰克语（日耳曼语族）表「占取、坐据」的词根；与 siege（围攻）同出一脉，均由「以力占取」之义生长，经英吉利法律用语定型为「扣押」。

sensesIntro.en: One snapping claw, five grips: the thief's arm, the capital, the assets, the nerves, the fleeting moment.
sensesIntro.cn: 一只猛合的爪子，五次抓握：小偷的手臂、首都、资产、神经与转瞬即逝的时机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a claw snapping shut around its prey
core.cn: 核心意象：利爪骤然合拢，钳住猎物

branches.en: the first physical snap of the hand
branches.cn: 手的第一次物理性抓合

branches.en: the snap scaled up to armies and cities
branches.cn: 爪子放大为军队与城市

branches.en: the grip wearing legal gloves
branches.cn: 戴上了法律手套的抓握

branches.en: the claw reaching into mind and body
branches.cn: 爪子伸进了心神与身体

branches.en: time itself caught in the grip
branches.cn: 连时间也被攥在爪中

intro.en: Words built on seize and its French-Germanic family.
intro.cn: 由 seize 及其法语-日耳曼词族构成的英语词。

latinIntro.en: No direct Latin cognates; the family is Germanic through French, so the list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 该词族经法语源自日耳曼语，无直接拉丁同源词，列表留空。

items.meaning: to grab or take by force
items.example: They seized the chance to expand.

items.meaning: the act of seizing or a medical fit
items.example: He had a seizure last night.

items.meaning: surrounding a place to capture it

items.example: The engine seized up in the cold.
items.exampleCN: 发动机在寒冷中卡住了。

items.meaningCN: 抓取——近义但词源不同，为本族词

items.exampleCN: 被没收的手机后来归还了。

definition_zh: 明智的；合理的；实用的
definition_en: showing good judgment; practical rather than emotional or extreme
core_image: 出门前看一眼天气预报再决定穿什么的人
scene: 出发前，她查了天气又检查了背包。 It is sensible to carry an umbrella in this season.
sceneCN: 这里 sensible 是「明智的；合理的」（第 1 个义项：显示出良好判断）；句意是这个季节带伞是明智之举。

derivatives.zh: sensible 加 -ly 副词后缀，义为「明智地；合理地」
sense 家族名词，义为「感受力；情感（常用复数）」
同族易混词，义为「敏感的」，与 sensible 区分

senses.title: Showing good judgment
senses.definition: acting or deciding in a reasonable way
senses.definitionCN: 以合理的方式行动或决定
senses.example: It was sensible to sell the shares early.
senses.exampleCN: 早点卖掉股票是明智的。
senses.why: The man checks the sky before every journey.
senses.whyCN: 此人每次上路前都先看看天。

senses.title: Practical rather than fancy
senses.definition: useful and plain instead of decorative or showy
senses.definitionCN: 朴素实用而不追求花哨
senses.example: She wore sensible boots for the farm visit.
senses.exampleCN: 参观农场时她穿了实用的靴子。
senses.why: The umbrella beats the silk hat when rain is promised.
senses.whyCN: 天气预报有雨时，伞胜过丝礼帽。

senses.title: Aware of something (formal or old use)
senses.definition: able to be felt or noticed
senses.definitionCN: 能被感觉到或注意到的（正式旧用法）
senses.example: He was sensible of the danger around him.
senses.exampleCN: 他察觉到四周的危险。
senses.why: The sky itself is felt, not seen, before the rain.
senses.whyCN: 落雨之前，天色是被感觉到的，而非被看见的。

senses.title: Reasonable in amount or degree
senses.definition: moderate and avoiding extremes
senses.definitionCN: 适度、不走极端
senses.example: Ask for a sensible price, not the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 要个合理的价格，别狮子大开口。
senses.why: The sky-watcher also knows when the rain is light enough to walk through.
senses.whyCN: 看天的人也知道，雨不大时可以直接走过。

intro.en: From Latin sensibilis, able to be felt, from sentire (to feel).
intro.cn: 来自拉丁语 sensibilis「可被感知的」，源于 sentire（感受）。

items.en: The direction-feeling root *sent- again underlies the family.
items.cn: 定向-感知词根 *sent- 同样支撑这个家族。

items.en: Sensibilis means capable of being sensed, from sensus with -ibilis.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sensibilis 由 sensus 加 -ibilis 构成，意为可被感知的。

items.en: Old French sensible carried both perceptible and emotional meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 sensible 兼有可感知与多情的含义。

items.en: English first used sensible for what can be felt.
items.cn: 英语起初用 sensible 表示可被感知之物。

items.en: By the 1700s the meaning shifted toward wise and practical judgment.
items.cn: 至十八世纪词义转向明智、务实的判断。

note.en: Look-alikes in the sensi- family, and near rivals in the judgment field.
note.cn: sensi- 词族的形近词，以及「判断」义场的近义词。

entries.definition: quick to feel or easily hurt
entries.definitionCN: 敏感的——同根易混：sensitive 感受多，sensible 判断准

entries.definition: emotional responsiveness
entries.definitionCN: 感受力——同族名词，注意与「明智」无关

entries.definition: never wrong
entries.definitionCN: 绝无差错的——拼写含 -ible 相近但词根不同

entries.definition: fair and logical
entries.definitionCN: 合理的——强调逻辑公道，sensible 强调务实

entries.definition: useful in real situations
entries.definitionCN: 实际的——与「实用」义项对应

entries.definition: having good judgment
entries.definitionCN: 明智的——更抽象，含经验智慧

normalIntro.en: Hooks on the sky-checker picture and the sensible-sensitive pair.
normalIntro.cn: 基于看天人画面与 sensible-sensitive 对的记忆钩子。

normal.en: sensible ends in -ible like visible: it can be judged by reason
normal.cn: sensible 以 -ible 收尾，如同 visible：可被理性把握

normal.en: sensitive feels, sensible decides: feel vs decide
normal.cn: sensitive 负责感受，sensible 负责决定

normal.en: sensible shoes are for walking, not showing
normal.cn: sensible shoes 用来走路，不是用来炫耀

normal.en: a sensible price stays near the ground
normal.cn: a sensible price 贴近地面，不飞上天

normal.en: the 18th-century meaning shift: from felt to wise
normal.cn: 十八世纪的词义转向：从「被感知」到「明智」

abstract.en: See a hand testing the wind before leaving home
abstract.cn: 看见出门前试探风力的那只手

abstract.en: Picture boots chosen for mud, not for mirrors
abstract.cn: 想象为泥泞而非为镜子选的靴子

abstract.en: Feel a decision landing quietly, without drama
abstract.cn: 体会一个决定安静落地、毫无戏剧性

examples.en: Buying insurance before the trip was a sensible move.
examples.cn: 出发前买保险是明智之举。

examples.en: He gave me some very sensible advice.
examples.cn: 他给了我非常合理的建议。

examples.en: Pack sensible clothes for the mountain trip.
examples.cn: 去山里要带上实用的衣物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 sens-爱布」——明智的人爱穿耐用的布鞋，不穿绣花鞋。

root: 拉丁语 sensibilis「可被感知的」（sensus 加 -ibilis），与 sense、sensitive、sensation 同根；英语中词义从「可感知的」逐步转向「判断明智的、务实的」，与 sensitive（感受多）形成分工。

sensesIntro.en: One sky-checker, four habits: deciding well, dressing plainly, feeling the air, and asking a fair price.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个看天的人，四种习惯：善做决定、衣着朴素、感知天色、索价公道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man glancing at the sky before stepping out
core.cn: 核心意象：出门前抬头看一眼天空的人

branches.en: the judgment shown in every step
branches.cn: 每一步都体现的判断力

branches.en: boots chosen for the road, not the mirror
branches.cn: 为路而非为镜选的靴子

branches.en: the old sense: felt before it is seen
branches.cn: 旧义：先被感知，后被看见

branches.en: a price that walks on the ground
branches.cn: 落在地面上的价格

branches.en: reason and practice in one glance at the sky
branches.cn: 理性与务实凝聚在看天的一瞥中

intro.en: Adjectives in the -ible family built on Latin feeling roots.
intro.cn: 由拉丁「感知」词根构成的 -ible 形容词家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives of sensibilis.
latinIntro.cn: sensibilis 的拉丁同族词。

items.example: Classical logic named the sensibilis world.
items.exampleCN: 古典逻辑把可感世界称为 sensibilis。

items.example: A sensible plan saved the day.
items.exampleCN: 明智的计划扭转了局面。

items.meaningCN: 可见的——同后缀但词根为 videre（看）
items.example: The tower is visible for miles.

items.meaningCN: 不会错的——形近异源，源自 fallere（欺骗）
items.exampleCN: 没有方法是万无一失的。

definition_zh: 包括；由…组成；构成
definition_en: to consist of particular parts, or to form a particular whole
core_image: 一只篮子里装着七种不同的水果，篮子本身不算在内
scene: 这支队伍由五名老队员和三名新人组成。 The team comprises five veterans and three newcomers.
sceneCN: 这里 comprise 指「由…组成」（第 1 个义项：整体包含所列的部分）；句意是这支队伍由五名老队员和三名新人组成。

senses.title: Consist of parts
senses.definition: to be made up of the parts that are mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 由所提到的部分构成
senses.example: The course comprises six modules.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程由六个模块组成。
senses.why: The whole stands first, and the parts are listed as its contents.
senses.whyCN: 整体先站在那里，部分则作为它的内容被列出。

senses.title: Form a whole together
senses.definition: to combine to form a particular whole
senses.definitionCN: 结合起来构成某个整体
senses.example: These six states comprise the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这六个州构成这个地区。
senses.why: Look from the other side and the parts are the builders of the whole.
senses.whyCN: 从另一面看，部分就是整体的建造者。

intro.en: Comprise comes from French comprendre, to include, and its past participle compris, meaning included.
intro.cn: comprise 来自法语 comprendre（包括），其过去分词 compris 意为被包括在内。

items.en: Comprehendere meant to seize or to take in.
items.cn: comprehendere 意为抓住或纳入。

items.en: Old French comprendre meant to contain or to include.
items.cn: 古法语 comprendre 意为包含或包括。

items.en: The past participle compris meant included in a whole.
items.cn: 过去分词 compris 意为被包括在整体中。

items.en: English comprise first meant to lay hold of or to include.
items.cn: 英语 comprise 最初指握住或包括。

items.en: It settled into the two opposite-looking patterns of whole and parts.
items.cn: 它最终固定为整体与部分两种看似相反的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to comprise, and the meaning group names other words for containing parts.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 comprise 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示包含部分的词。

entries.definition: to form a whole from parts
an agreement in which each side gives up something
an unexpected event or feeling
to have something as one of its parts
to have something inside
to include something as part of a whole

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a basket full of fruit, then look at the same basket from the fruit's side.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从装满水果的篮子开始，再从水果那一侧看同一只篮子。

normal.en: Com- is together and prise comes from prendre, to take, so comprise is to take things together.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，prise 源自 prendre（拿取），comprise 就是把东西一起收进来。

normal.en: A team comprises its members; the members compose the team.
normal.cn: 队伍 comprise 队员，而队员 compose 队伍。

normal.en: Do not say is comprised by; use is composed of instead.
normal.cn: 不要说 is comprised by，而用 is composed of 更稳妥。

normal.en: The whole comprises the parts, never the other way round.
normal.cn: 整体 comprise 部分，而不是反过来。

normal.en: A region comprises its states, and the states make up the region.
normal.cn: 地区 comprise 各州，而各州构成了地区。

abstract.en: Picture a basket holding seven different fruits.
abstract.cn: 想象一只篮子装着七种不同的水果。

abstract.en: Picture a single box with every item listed on its side.
abstract.cn: 想象一只箱子，侧面列着里面每样东西。

abstract.en: Picture a circle drawn around several separate dots.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圆圈把几个分开的点圈在一起。

examples.en: The committee comprises twelve members.
examples.cn: 委员会由十二名成员组成。

examples.en: These four counties comprise the whole province.
examples.cn: 这四个县构成整个省。

examples.en: The price comprises room and breakfast.
examples.cn: 价格包括房费和早餐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 comprise 记成 com（一起）加 prise（拿取）：把一个整体里的部分一起拿进来，就是包括、由…组成。

root: 源自拉丁语 comprehendere（抓住、纳入）经法语 comprendre 与过去分词 compris 进入英语，本义是把部分收进整体，后指由…组成与构成。

sensesIntro.en: From a whole taking in its parts, to the parts building that whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 从整体把部分收进来，到部分建成那个整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one basket holding seven kinds of fruit, with the basket itself not counted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只篮子装着七种水果，篮子本身不计在内。

branches.en: The whole containing its parts is the usual modern sense.
branches.cn: 整体包含部分，是常见的现代义项。

branches.en: The parts forming the whole is the same fact seen from below.
branches.cn: 部分构成整体，是从下往上看同一件事。

branches.en: A course or a team is described from the whole side.
branches.cn: 课程或队伍通常从整体这一侧描述。

branches.en: A group of states is described from the parts side.
branches.cn: 一组州则从部分这一侧描述。

branches.en: Both patterns describe one relation of container and contents.
branches.cn: 两种句式描述的都是容器与内容的关系。

intro.en: Comprise is built on Latin com-, together, plus prehendere, to take, through the French past participle compris.
intro.cn: comprise 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 prehendere（拿取）构成，经法语过去分词 compris 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base prehend- also gives comprehend and comprehensive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 prehend- 还给出 comprehend 与 comprehensive。

items.example: The group is comprised of ten firms.
items.exampleCN: 这个集团由十家公司组成。

items.example: A panel comprising five judges will decide.
items.exampleCN: 一个由五名评委组成的小组将作出裁定。

items.example: The comprisal of all costs took time.
items.exampleCN: 把所有费用都包括进去花了些时间。

items.meaning: the way parts form a whole
items.example: The composition of the panel changed.

items.meaning: to form a whole from parts

items.example: The panel is a composite structure.
A comprehensive list would be long.
items.exampleCN: 一份全面的清单会很长。

definition_zh: 意识；认识；察觉
definition_en: the state of knowing that something exists or is important
core_image: 一束灯光照亮原本黑暗的角落
scene: 社区公告栏前围了一圈人。 The campaign raised awareness of water waste.
sceneCN: 这里 awareness 是「意识」（第 1 个义项：知道某事存在或重要）；句意是这场活动提高了人们对水资源浪费的意识。

senses.title: The state of knowing
senses.definition: the state of knowing that something exists
senses.definitionCN: 知道某事存在的状态
senses.example: The campaign raised awareness of water waste.
senses.exampleCN: 这场活动提高了人们对水资源浪费的意识。
senses.why: Awareness is aware plus -ness, and the suffix turns a passing state of attention into a lasting condition of mind.
senses.whyCN: awareness 是 aware 加 -ness，后缀把一时的注意变成一种持续的心智状态。

senses.title: Public understanding
senses.definition: the extent to which people know and care about an issue
senses.definitionCN: 人们对某个议题了解与关心的程度
senses.example: Public awareness of the disease has grown.
senses.exampleCN: 公众对这种疾病的认识提高了。
senses.why: When many people hold the same knowledge, awareness becomes a social measure rather than a private feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人共享同一种认识时，awareness 就从私人感受变成了社会性的衡量指标。

intro.en: Awareness is the noun built on the old word for watchfulness.
intro.cn: awareness 是建在古「警觉」一词上的名词。

items.en: wær meant 'watchful'.
items.cn: wær 意为「警觉的」。

items.en: aware meant 'watchful, then knowing'.
items.cn: aware 意为「警觉的，后为知道的」。

items.en: The suffix -ness made a state noun.
items.cn: 后缀 -ness 构成表示状态的名词。

items.en: awareness meant the state of being aware.
items.cn: awareness 意为「觉察的状态」。

items.en: It also names public attention to issues.
items.cn: 如今也指公众对议题的关注。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the aware base; the near-meaning group gives kinds of mental attention.
note.cn: 形近组都含 aware 词基；近义组是表示心理注意的词。

normalIntro.en: Awareness is watchfulness made permanent and shared.
normalIntro.cn: awareness 是警觉被固定下来，并被许多人共享。

normal.en: Awareness is uncountable, so it takes no plural.
normal.cn: awareness 不可数，没有复数。

normal.en: Awareness of something names the thing noticed.

abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照亮房间里黑暗的一角。

definition_zh: 得到；源自；推导出
definition_en: to get something from a source, or to come from a particular origin
core_image: 一条小溪从岩缝里渗出，顺着山势往下越流越宽
scene: 老师带学生沿河往上游走，最后停在山脚一处小小的泉眼边。 Many English words derive from Latin roots.
sceneCN: 这里 derive 指「源自」（第 2 个义项：从某个源头而来）；句意是许多英语单词源自拉丁词根。

senses.title: Get something from a source
senses.definition: to get something such as pleasure, income or knowledge from a particular source
senses.definitionCN: 从某一来源获得乐趣、收入或知识等
senses.example: She derives great pleasure from teaching children.
senses.exampleCN: 她从教孩子这件事上得到很大乐趣。
senses.why: The good thing is not made on the spot; it flows in from somewhere else.
senses.whyCN: 好处并非当场造出，而是从别处流进来的。

senses.title: Come from an origin
senses.definition: to come from or have its origin in something
senses.definitionCN: 从某事物而来，以其为起源
senses.example: Many English words derive from Latin roots.
senses.exampleCN: 许多英语单词源自拉丁词根。
senses.why: Every stream can be followed back to the spring that fed it.
senses.whyCN: 每条溪流都能顺水追到供它水的那眼泉。

senses.title: Reach by reasoning
senses.definition: to reach a result by reasoning from facts or rules already known
senses.definitionCN: 依据已知事实或规则推理得出结果
senses.example: We can derive the answer from these two simple rules.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以从这两条简单规则推出答案。
senses.why: Reasoning is a channel cut from known ground to a new result.
senses.whyCN: 推理就是从已知的地面开一条渠，通向新的结果。

intro.en: Derive comes from Latin derivare, to lead water away from a stream, built on de- and rivus, a stream, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: derive 来自拉丁语 derivare，本义是把水从河里引走，由 de- 与 rivus（小河）构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Rivus named a stream, and derivare meant to lead its water into a new channel.
items.cn: rivus 指小河，derivare 指把河水引进新的渠道。

items.en: Writers extended it from water to words, arguing that one form flows from another.
items.cn: 作家把它从水移到语言上，说一个形式是从另一个形式流出来的。

items.en: French deriver carried the sense of coming from a source.
items.cn: 法语 deriver 带着「自某处而来」的意思。

items.en: English took it up for both obtaining something and tracing an origin.
items.cn: 英语用它同时表示获得某物与追溯来源。

items.en: Science added the mathematical sense of working a result out from rules.
items.cn: 科学又添上从规则算出结果的数学义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -rive sound, while the meaning group runs from starting somewhere to getting and inferring.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -rive 这一段音，近义组则从发源一路走到获得与推断。

entries.definition: to take something away from someone
a form or thing that comes from another
entries.definitionCN: 由另一形式或事物派生的东西

entries.definition: the origin or formation of a word
to begin to exist in a particular place
to get something that you want
to reach a conclusion by reasoning

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with water leaving a spring and end with a rule that yields an answer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从水离开泉眼开始，落到一条算出答案的规则。

normal.en: A river and a word both have a spring somewhere upstream.
normal.cn: 河与词，上游都有一眼泉。

normal.en: To derive is to follow the water back, not to invent it.
normal.cn: derive 是顺着水往回找，而不是凭空造水。

normal.en: Pleasure, profit and meaning can all be led into your own field.
normal.cn: 乐趣、收益与意义，都能被引进你自己的田里。

normal.en: The Latin root rivus is a stream, and the word still flows.
normal.cn: 拉丁词基 rivus 是小河，这个词至今还在流。

normal.en: A formula is a channel dug from known facts to a new result.
normal.cn: 公式就是从已知事实挖向新结果的一条渠。

abstract.en: Picture a hand cupping water where it seeps from rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在岩缝渗水处捧起一汪水。

abstract.en: Picture a map where every small tributary points back to one dot.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，每条小支流都指向同一个点。

abstract.en: Picture a proof written line by line until the last line lands.
abstract.cn: 想象一份证明一行行写下去，直到最后一行落定。

examples.en: Many English words derive from Latin roots.
examples.cn: 许多英语单词源自拉丁词根。

examples.en: She derived great pleasure from teaching children.
examples.cn: 她从教孩子这件事上得到很大乐趣。

examples.en: The formula can be derived from two simple rules.
examples.cn: 这个公式可以由两条简单规则推导出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 derive 记成「得瑞武」：de 像「得」，rive 像「河」，从河里得到水，就是获得与源自。

root: 来自拉丁语 derivare，本义是把水从小河里引走，由 de-（离开）与 rivus（小河）组成，经法语 dériver 进入英语。后来从引水引申为获得好处，又引申为追溯来源与推理推导。

sensesIntro.en: From water led out of a stream, to a word traced to its root, to a result reached by rule.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把水从河里引出，到把一个词追到词根，再到按规则推出结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stream led out of its old channel into a new one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股水被引出旧河道，流进新渠道。

branches.en: The first sense is what the new channel brings you.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是新渠道带给你的东西。

branches.en: The second sense is the spring that every channel starts from.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是每条渠道起步的那眼泉。

branches.en: The third sense is a channel dug by reasoning alone.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是单靠推理挖出的渠道。

branches.en: Getting and coming from are the two ends of one flow.
branches.cn: 获得与源自，是同一条水流的上下游两端。

branches.en: A word traced to its root and a result traced to its rules use the same backward walk.
branches.cn: 词追到词根、结果追到规则，用的是同一种往回走的步子。

intro.en: Derive has a small Latin family built on a stream and on the act of leading water away.
intro.cn: derive 有一小族拉丁词，建在「小河」与「引水」这两件事上。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin rivus, a stream, and de- adds the sense of away or down.

items.meaning: the act of getting from a source

definition_zh: 成功的；有成就的
definition_en: achieving the results you wanted, or having gained wealth or a high position
core_image: 把想法一点点做成现实，最后举杯庆祝
scene: 这家小店的生意越来越好。 The little shop has become very successful.
sceneCN: 这里 successful 是「成功的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家小店的生意越来越好。

senses.title: Achieving
senses.definition: achieving the results you wanted
senses.definitionCN: 达到预期结果
senses.example: The experiment was successful.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验是成功的。
senses.why: This is the main sense of reaching a goal.
senses.whyCN: 这是达成目标的主要义项。

senses.title: Prosperous
senses.definition: having gained wealth or a high position
senses.definitionCN: 获得了财富或较高地位
senses.example: She is a successful lawyer.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位很有成就的律师。
senses.why: Here success is measured by status and wealth.
senses.whyCN: 这里用地位和财富衡量成功。

senses.title: Well received
senses.definition: popular with many people
senses.definitionCN: 受到很多人欢迎的
senses.example: The film was successful at the box office.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影票房很好。
senses.why: A work is called successful when crowds like it.
senses.whyCN: 作品受大众喜爱时也被称为成功。

definition_zh: 尺寸；维度；方面；规模
definition_en: a measurement of length, width or height, or one part of a situation
core_image: 一只木箱被卷尺量过三次，长、宽、高各贴一张小纸条
scene: 木匠把卷尺拉开，沿箱子的三条边各量一次。 The room's dimensions are printed on the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 dimensions 指「尺寸」（第 1 个义项：长宽高的大小）；句意是这个房间的尺寸印在图纸上。

senses.title: A measured size
senses.definition: a length, width or height that can be measured
senses.definitionCN: 可以量出来的长、宽或高
senses.example: Check the dimensions before you buy the table.
senses.exampleCN: 买桌子之前先看尺寸。
senses.why: A thing in space always asks to be measured in more than one way.
senses.whyCN: 空间里的东西，总要被不止一种方式量过。

senses.title: One direction in space
senses.definition: one of the directions in which space or a model extends
senses.definitionCN: 空间或模型伸展的某一个方向
senses.example: A line has only one dimension.
senses.exampleCN: 一条线只有一个维度。
senses.why: Counting the directions turns a shape into a number.
senses.whyCN: 把方向数出来，形状就变成了一个数。

senses.title: One side of a matter
senses.definition: one part of a situation that must be considered
senses.definitionCN: 一件事中必须被考虑到的一面
senses.example: The story has a moral dimension as well.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事还有道德层面。
senses.why: Problems have depth too, and each depth is called a dimension.
senses.whyCN: 问题也有厚度，每一层厚度都叫一个维度。

intro.en: Dimension comes from Latin dimensio, a measuring out, from metiri, to measure.
intro.cn: dimension 来自拉丁语 dimensio（量出），词根是 metiri（测量）。

items.en: Metiri meant to measure land or length.
items.cn: metiri 指丈量土地或长度。

items.en: Dimetiri meant to measure out in full.
items.cn: dimetiri 指完整地量出。

items.en: Dimensio named the result of that measuring.
items.cn: dimensio 指量过之后得到的结果。

items.en: English dimension meant size as measured.
items.cn: 英语 dimension 指量出来的大小。

items.en: Science added the sense of an axis, and common use added the sense of an aspect.
items.cn: 科学添上「坐标轴」的意思，日常用法又添上「方面」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the men- sound, while the meaning group covers size, aspect and extent.
note.cn: 形近组共用 men 这一段音，近义组则覆盖大小、方面与范围。

abstract.en: Picture three chalk marks at right angles.
abstract.cn: 想象三道互相垂直的粉笔线。

abstract.en: Picture a flat drawing that suddenly gains depth.
abstract.cn: 想象一张平面图忽然有了厚度。

examples.en: The sofa fits the dimensions of the room.
examples.cn: 这张沙发与房间的尺寸相合。

examples.en: Time is often called the fourth dimension.
examples.cn: 时间常被称作第四维。

examples.en: Her letter added a personal dimension to the case.
examples.cn: 她的来信为这个案子添了个人层面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dimension 记成「地门神」：门口的地要量一量，量出长宽高，就是尺寸。

root: 来自拉丁语 dimensio，词根 metiri 意为测量，前缀 di- 表示分开、逐项。本义是逐项量出的结果，即长宽高等尺寸；数学与物理把它抽象为「维度」，日常语言又把它引申为事情的「方面」与「规模」。

sensesIntro.en: From a tape laid along a box, to an axis in space, to a side of a question that must be weighed.
sensesIntro.cn: 从贴着箱子的卷尺，到空间中的一根轴，再到一个问题必须被衡量的那一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three tape marks at right angles on one wooden box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只木箱上三道互相垂直的卷尺痕。

branches.en: The first sense is the measured size of a thing.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是东西被量出来的大小。

branches.en: The second sense is a direction in space.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是空间里的一个方向。

branches.en: The third sense is a side of a situation.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是事情的一个面。

branches.en: Measuring a box and naming an axis use the same idea.
branches.cn: 量一只箱子与命名一根轴，用的是同一个想法。

branches.en: Depth in space becomes depth in meaning.
branches.cn: 空间里的深度，变成了意思上的深度。

intro.en: Dimension joins a family of measuring words built on the Latin root metiri.
intro.cn: dimension 加入一族表示测量的词，词根是拉丁语 metiri。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin metiri, to measure, seen also in metre and measure.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 metiri（测量），metre 与 measure 里也能看到它。

items.example: The dimension of the box surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 这只箱子的尺寸让我们意外。

items.example: Write the dimensions on the label.
The two shapes are dimensionally equal.
items.exampleCN: 这两个形状在尺寸上相等。
贫困是个多层面的问题。

items.meaning: to find the size of something
items.example: Measure the wall before buying paint.
The room is four metres wide.

definition_zh: 评论；意见；注释；评论（动词）
definition_en: a spoken or written remark about someone or something, a note explaining a text, or to make such a remark
core_image: 看完文章后在页边写下的一行小字
scene: 视频下面，网友留下一条简短的评价。 He read the comment and smiled.
sceneCN: 这里 comment 指「评论；意见」（第 1 个义项：对事物的看法）；句意是他读了那条评论，笑了笑。

senses.title: A remark
senses.definition: something that you say or write to give your opinion
senses.definitionCN: 为表达看法而说或写的话
senses.example: He made a kind comment about her cooking.
senses.exampleCN: 他对她的厨艺说了句善意的评论。
senses.why: The everyday sense is a short remark offered to others.
senses.whyCN: 最日常的义项就是向别人说出的简短评语。

senses.title: A note explaining a text
senses.definition: a note added to a text to explain a difficult word or passage
senses.definitionCN: 加在文本旁解释难词或难句的注记
senses.example: The editor added a comment in the margin.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑在页边加了一条注释。
senses.why: Scholars first wrote comments beside old books to explain them.
senses.whyCN: 学者最早在古书旁写注，用来解释原文。

senses.title: To remark
senses.definition: to say something that gives your opinion about a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 说出对某人或某事的看法
senses.example: Several readers commented on the article.
senses.exampleCN: 几位读者对这篇文章发表了评论。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to offer a comment.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：把一条评论给出去。

intro.en: Comment comes from Latin commentum, a note or invention, built on comminisci, to devise.
intro.cn: comment 来自拉丁语 commentum（注记、构想），源自 comminisci（想出、构思）。

items.en: Comminisci meant to think up or devise something.
items.cn: comminisci 意为想出或构思出某物。

items.en: Commentum named a written note that explained a text.
items.cn: commentum 指解释文本的书面注记。

items.en: Old French coment kept the scholarly sense of a note.
items.cn: 古法语 coment 保留了注记的学术含义。

items.en: English comment first meant an explanatory note.
items.cn: 英语 comment 最初指解释性的注释。

items.en: It widened to any remark of opinion, spoken or posted online.
items.cn: 它的范围扩展到任何表达看法的话，无论口说还是网上发布。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape to comment, while the meaning group gives other words for a remark.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 comment 形状相近的词，近义组给出其他表示评语的词。

entries.definition: an icy body that moves around the sun
to begin something formal
a powder that hardens when mixed with water
something you say to express a thought
a spoken or written note based on watching
a short written record or explanation

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a line written in a margin, then move to remarks about people and to posting a reply online.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从页边写下的一行字开始，再走到对人的评语与网上发帖回复。

normal.en: A comment is short by nature: one thought, one line.
normal.cn: 评论天生简短：一个想法，一行字。

normal.en: No comment is a complete answer in the news world.
normal.cn: 在新闻界，无可奉告就是一个完整的回答。

normal.en: Comment on takes the topic after on, not after of.
normal.cn: 表示评论某事时，用 comment on 而不是 of。

normal.en: Commentary is the long version, commentator is the person.
normal.cn: commentary 是长篇的评论，commentator 是评论的人。

normal.en: Margins of old books are full of comments in faded ink.
normal.cn: 古书的页边写满了褪色墨水的注释。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil writing a small note beside a hard sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔在一个难句旁写下小注。

abstract.en: Picture a screen filling with short replies under a video.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一个视频下方涌满简短回复。

abstract.en: Picture a reporter waiting and receiving only silence.
abstract.cn: 想象记者等着，却只得到沉默。

examples.en: Her comment on the plan was short and kind.
examples.cn: 她对这份计划的评论简短而友善。

examples.en: The teacher wrote a comment beside each essay.
examples.cn: 老师在每篇作文旁写了批注。

examples.en: Many readers commented under the story.
examples.cn: 许多读者在报道下面发表了评论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 comment 记成「写在小纸条上的话」：看完别人的东西，随手留一句，就是评论。

root: 源自拉丁语 commentum（注记、构想），出自 comminisci（想出），本义是在文本旁写下的解释，后泛指一切表达看法的话。

sensesIntro.en: From a note in the margin, to a remark about a person, and finally to posting an opinion online.
sensesIntro.cn: 从页边的注记，到对人的评语，再到网上发布看法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of small handwriting added beside a printed page.
core.cn: 核心意象：看完文章后在页边写下的一行小字。

branches.en: A short remark is the sense used most today.
branches.cn: 简短的评语是今天用得最多的义项。

branches.en: The scholarly margin note is the oldest written sense.
branches.cn: 学术性的页边注是最早的书面义项。

branches.en: The verb simply means to put a comment into words.
branches.cn: 动词义就是把一条评论说出来。

branches.en: Both a spoken remark and a written note add a voice to a text.
branches.cn: 口头的评语与书面的注记，都是给文本添上一个声音。

branches.en: Noun and verb differ only in whether the remark is out yet.
branches.cn: 名词与动词的差别，只在于那句话有没有说出口。

intro.en: Comment grows into a family with -ary, -ator and -ate, all about explaining or judging.
intro.cn: comment 靠 -ary、-ator 与 -ate 长成一个家族，都与解释或评判有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin commentum links the word to mental invention as well as to notes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 commentum 把这个词同时连向头脑的构想与书面的注记。

items.structure: plural noun and third person singular
items.example: The page received hundreds of comments.
items.exampleCN: 这个页面收到了数百条评论。

items.example: She commented that the room was too warm.
He was commenting on the match.

items.meaning: a continuous explanation or set of comments
items.example: The radio commentary described every pass.
items.exampleCN: 电台解说描述了每一次传球。

items.meaning: a person who comments, especially on events
items.exampleCN: 解说员认识每一位球员。

items.meaning: to describe an event as it happens
the place where sports commentators sit
items.example: The commentary box overlooks the field.

items.meaning: a person who leaves comments online
items.example: One commenter asked a fair question.
items.exampleCN: 一位留言者提了个公允的问题。

definition_zh: 抱怨；投诉；疾病
definition_en: a statement that you are not satisfied, or an illness that troubles you
core_image: 信箱里塞着一张写满字的意见卡
scene: 客房的空调响个不停，前台记下房号并派人上去。 The hotel received three complaints about the lift.
sceneCN: 这里 complaint 指「投诉」（第 2 个义项：正式反映问题）；句意是酒店收到三条关于电梯的投诉。

senses.title: A statement of dissatisfaction
senses.definition: a statement that something is wrong or annoying
senses.definitionCN: 说明某事有问题或令人烦的话
senses.example: My main complaint is the noise at night.
senses.exampleCN: 我主要的抱怨是夜里的噪音。
senses.why: The noun holds the words that the verb lets out.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词装着动词说出口的那些话。

senses.title: A formal protest
senses.definition: an official statement that something is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 向管理方正式说明问题的陈述
senses.example: She filed a complaint with the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 她向经理提交了投诉。
senses.why: Written down and handed to someone with power, a grumble becomes a case.
senses.whyCN: 写下来交给有权处理的人，嘟囔就成了一桩案子。

senses.title: An illness
senses.definition: an illness or a pain in part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 身体某处的病或疼痛
senses.example: The doctor asked about her stomach complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 医生问起她的胃病。
senses.why: A long tradition calls the body's troubles a complaint of the flesh.
senses.whyCN: 很久以来的说法把身体的不适称作肉身的抱怨。

intro.en: Complaint comes from Old French complainte, a noun of lament built on Latin plangere, to beat the breast.
intro.cn: complaint 来自古法语 complainte，这个表示哀叹的名词建立在拉丁语 plangere（捶胸）之上。

items.en: Plangere meant to strike the breast in sorrow.
items.cn: plangere 意为悲伤地捶胸。

items.en: Plangere widened to any loud grieving.
items.cn: plangere 扩展到任何出声的悲悼。

items.en: Old French complainte named the lament itself.
items.cn: 古法语 complainte 指哀叹这件事本身。

items.en: English complaint first meant a lament for a loss.
items.cn: 英语 complaint 最初指为损失而哀叹。

items.en: It came to mean a grumble, a formal case and a bodily illness.
items.cn: 后来它指抱怨、正式案件以及身体的不适。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words one step from complaint, and the meaning group separates a grievance, an objection and an illness.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 complaint 只差一步的词，近义组分辨不满申诉、异议与疾病。

entries.definition: to say you are unhappy
to finish something
a contest or rivalry
a formal reason for complaint
a statement of disagreement
a disease or a period of bad health

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a full suggestion box, then move to an official case and to a sickness that has a name.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从塞满的意见箱开始，再走到正式的案子以及有了名字的病。

normal.en: Complaint is what is left after someone has complained.
normal.cn: complaint 就是有人抱怨过之后留下来的东西。

normal.en: Make a complaint, file a complaint, lodge a complaint: all three are common.
normal.cn: 提出、提交、正式递交投诉，三种说法都常见。

normal.en: A minor complaint at the doctor is a small illness.
normal.cn: 在医生那里说的小 complaint，就是小毛病。

normal.en: The spelling changes from complain to complaint; keep the t.
normal.cn: 从 complain 变 complaint 时要留住结尾的 t。

normal.en: A complaint is a complaint whether it is spoken, written or felt in the body.
normal.cn: 无论说出口、写下来还是落在身体里，它都是 complaint。

abstract.en: Picture a card box so full that the lid will not shut.
abstract.cn: 想象意见卡多到盒盖合不上。

abstract.en: Picture a form with a room number written in the corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格，角上写着房间号。

abstract.en: Picture a patient listing symptoms one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象病人一条条说出症状。

examples.en: The manager listened to every complaint politely.
examples.cn: 经理礼貌地听完每一条投诉。

examples.en: He made a complaint about the broken seat.
examples.cn: 他就坏掉的座位提出了投诉。

examples.en: Her only complaint was a mild cough.
examples.cn: 她唯一的不适是轻微的咳嗽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 complaint 记成 complain（抱怨）加 t：抱怨说出口，变成一件事，就是投诉。

root: 源自古法语 complainte，出自拉丁语 plangere（捶胸），本义是哀叹之声，后引申为抱怨、投诉与身体的不适。

sensesIntro.en: From a voiced grumble, to an official case, and finally to an illness of the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 从说出口的嘟囔，到正式的案子，最后到身体的不适。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a complaint card crammed into a small hotel letterbox.
core.cn: 核心意象：信箱里塞着一张写满字的意见卡。

branches.en: The spoken grumble is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 说出口的嘟囔是日常义项。

branches.en: Written and filed, the grumble becomes a case.
branches.cn: 写下来归档，嘟囔就成了一桩案子。

branches.en: The body also makes complaints, and doctors name them.
branches.cn: 身体也会抱怨，医生给它们命名。

branches.en: Both are words pointed at something wrong.
branches.cn: 两者都是指向某个问题的言语。

branches.en: Both are recorded, one on paper and one in a file of health.
branches.cn: 两者都会被记录，一个记在纸上，一个记在病历里。

intro.en: Complaint is the noun matching the verb complain, formed with a final -t.
intro.cn: complaint 是与动词 complain 对应的名词，以结尾的 -t 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin lament base plangere also survives in plangent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示哀叹的词基 plangere 也留在 plangent 里。

items.example: The office handles hundreds of complaints.
items.exampleCN: 这个办公室处理数百条投诉。

items.meaning: says he or she is unhappy
the person who files a complaint
items.example: The complainant gave a short statement.

definition_zh: 任命；委派；约定；指定；确定时间；（古）布置；装备
definition_en: to name someone for a position, to fix a time or place by agreement, or to furnish and equip
core_image: 在名册上某个名字旁边落下一笔，把人和位置钉在一起
scene: 董事会散会后，主席在走廊上停下脚步宣布人选。 The board appointed her as the new director of research.
sceneCN: 这里 appoint 是「任命；委派」（第 1 个义项：把某人指定到某个职位上）；句意为「董事会任命她为新的研究主管」。画面里有散会的成员、长长的走廊与主席手中的名册。

pos.zh: 动词：任命；委派；约定；指定；确定；（古）布置

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「约会；任命；职位」
由本词加 -ee 构成，义为「被任命者」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「约定的；被任命的」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「由任命产生的」

senses.title: To name someone for a post
senses.definition: to officially choose someone for a job, office, or duty
senses.definitionCN: 正式选定某人担任某项工作、职务或职责
senses.example: The board appointed her as the new director of research.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会任命她为新的研究主管。
senses.why: Old French apointer put a person at a point, and a post is exactly such a point in an organization.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 apointer 把人放到某个点上，而职位正是组织里的这样一个点。

senses.title: To fix a time or place
senses.definition: to arrange or fix a time and place for something by agreement
senses.definitionCN: 经双方同意安排或确定某事的时间与地点
senses.example: They appointed a day for the next meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他们约定了下次会议的日期。
senses.why: A time is also a point on the calendar; to appoint it is to fix it by agreement.
senses.whyCN: 时间也是日历上的一个点；约定时间就是经双方同意把它固定下来。

senses.title: Something settled in advance
senses.definition: in phrases such as the appointed hour, a time or place already fixed
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the appointed hour 一类说法，指已经确定的时间或地点
senses.example: The appointed hour came and no one arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 约定的时间到了，却没有人来。
senses.why: Once a point is fixed, whatever is to happen at it has been decided in advance.
senses.whyCN: 一个点一旦被固定，在这个点上要发生什么就被预先决定了。

senses.title: To furnish and equip
senses.definition: to supply a room or building with furniture and equipment, an older use of the word
senses.definitionCN: 为房间或建筑配置家具与设备，属于较古的用法
senses.example: The hall was appointed with heavy oak tables.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里配置了厚重的橡木桌。
senses.why: The older sense furnished a place by placing each item at its proper point.
senses.whyCN: 较古的义项是把每件东西放到它应在的位置上，从而布置好一个地方。

intro.en: Appoint comes from the French phrase for putting something at a point, and the point is still visible in its senses.
intro.cn: appoint 来自法语中「把某物放到一个点上」的说法，那个点至今仍留在它的各个义项里。

items.en: 「*peuǵ-」 'to prick, point' is the reconstructed root behind the point words; its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 原始印欧语「*peuǵ-」意为「刺、点」，是这一族「点」类词的根源；更早的来源存疑。

items.en: Punctum means 'a point, a prick', from the verb pungere 'to prick'.
items.cn: punctum 意为「点、刺痕」，来自动词 pungere「刺」。

items.en: French point means both a point and a fixed spot or moment.
items.cn: 法语 point 既指一个点，也指固定的地点或时刻。

items.en: Apointer, 'to put at a point, to arrange', gives English appoint in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: apointer 意为「放到一个点上、安排」，十四世纪时进入英语成为 appoint。

items.en: The sense of naming someone to a post dominates; the older sense of furnishing survives only in old texts.
items.cn: 任命某人担任职位的义项占了主导；较古的布置义只留在旧文献里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the appointment family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of choosing and fixing.
note.cn: 形近组收 appoint 的派生词族；近义组收表示挑选与确定的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a meeting or a named post.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词派生的名词，义为「约会」或「任命、职位」。

entries.definition: A person who has been chosen for a post.
To fail to meet someone's hope or expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使失望」，由 dis- 加 appoint 构成。

entries.definition: To propose someone formally for a post or award.
entries.definitionCN: 正式提名某人担任职位或获奖，比 appoint 少一层最终决定。

entries.definition: To mark out or name someone for a particular purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 指定或标明某人用于某用途，与 appoint 的指定义接近。

entries.definition: To give a task or place to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 把任务或位置分派给某人，比 appoint 更偏分工。

entries.definition: To fix a time for an event in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 预先为某事定下时间，对应 appoint 的约定义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks all return to the picture of a point on a page or a calendar.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都回到纸面或日历上的一个点。

normal.en: A point is the heart of the word: appoint means put at a point.
normal.cn: 点是这个词的核心：appoint 就是把某物放到一个点上。

normal.en: Put a name at the point of a post, and you have appointed someone.
normal.cn: 把名字放到职位这个点上，你就任命了某人。

normal.en: Put a meeting at a point on the calendar, and you have appointed a day.
normal.cn: 把会议放到日历上的一个点，你就约定了日期。

normal.en: At the appointed time, the point has already been fixed.
normal.cn: 到了约定时间，那个点早已固定。

normal.en: The old sense put furniture at its points too.
normal.cn: 较古的义项也是把家具放到各自的点位上。

abstract.en: A point can hold a name, a moment, or a piece of furniture.
abstract.cn: 一个点可以放名字、放时刻，也可以放一件家具。

abstract.en: Appointing is always an act of fixing: who, when, where.
abstract.cn: 任命与约定都是一种固定：定人、定时、定地。

abstract.en: The word turns empty space into an order.
abstract.cn: 这个词把空处变成一个秩序。

examples.en: The board appointed her as the new director of research.
examples.cn: 董事会任命她为新的研究主管。

examples.en: They appointed a day for the next meeting.
examples.cn: 他们约定了下次会议的日期。

examples.en: The appointed hour came and no one arrived.
examples.cn: 约定的时间到了，却没有人来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿波因特」——主席在名册名字旁点一个点，把他钉到职位上：任命

root: appoint 来自古法语 apointer「放到一个点上、安排」，其源头是拉丁语 punctum「点」，再往上可追到表示「刺、点」的印欧词根，确切形式存疑。十四世纪进入英语后，这个词始终围绕「把一个点固定下来」：把名字放到职位这个点上就是任命，把会议放到日历这个点上就是约定，把时间地点提前钉死就是指定的，而较古的用法是把家具各放到应在的点位上，也就是布置。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses all fix something at a point: a person to a post, a meeting to a day, an hour already settled, and furniture placed in a room.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法都把某物固定在一个点上：把人定到职位，把会议定到某日，把时间提前钉死，以及把家具摆进房间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen touching a name on a roster, pinning a person to a place.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔尖落在名册的一个名字旁，把一个人钉在一个位置上。

branches.en: THE POST LINE: a name is fixed to a position.
branches.cn: 职位线：一个名字被固定到一个职位上。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR LINE: a meeting is fixed to a day.
branches.cn: 日历线：一场会议被固定到某一天。

branches.en: THE FIXED POINT LINE: once set, the hour cannot move.
branches.cn: 定点线：一旦定下，那个时刻不能再移动。

branches.en: THE ROOM LINE: each item is placed at its proper point.
branches.cn: 房间线：每件东西被放到它应在的位置。

branches.en: THE ORDER LINE: people and times are arranged into a plan.
branches.cn: 秩序线：人与时间被编排进一个计划。

intro.en: Appoint is a verb borrowed whole from French; its endings multiply through suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: appoint 是从法语整体借来的动词，它的词形靠后缀与复合不断增殖。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer sits one step back: punctum 'point' lies behind the French word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层退在一步之后：punctum「点」位于法语词背后。

items.meaning: to send someone to a post

items.meaning: claiming a role without being chosen
items.example: He became the self-appointed guide of the group.
items.exampleCN: 他成了这群人自封的向导。

scene: 她在街角杂货店买牛奶。 She bought milk at the grocery.

senses.title: Food shop
senses.definition: a shop that sells food and small household goods

senses.example: She bought milk at the grocery.

senses.why: This is the common American sense.

senses.title: Food bought
senses.definition: the food and goods bought at such a shop, usually plural
senses.definitionCN: 在此类商店买到的食品和杂货，常用复数
senses.example: The groceries are in the kitchen.

senses.why: The shop name shifted to what it sells.

senses.title: The trade
senses.definition: the business of selling food goods
senses.definitionCN: 销售食品杂货的行业
senses.example: He has worked in grocery for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在杂货业干了很多年。
senses.why: The abstract trade sense names the whole field.

intro.en: Grocery comes from Old French grosserie, wholesale trade, from Medieval Latin grosseria.

items.cn: grossus 意为大的、粗的。

items.en: Grocery named the trade in bulk goods.

definition_zh: 建筑学；建筑术；建筑风格；建筑作品；体系结构
definition_en: the art and study of designing buildings; the style of buildings; or the overall structure of a system
core_image: 一张总平面图，石头、拱线与空间按同一秩序排开
scene: 老城街头，游客仰头看着一排石拱。 She studied the architecture of the old town for her thesis.
sceneCN: 这里 architecture 是「建筑风格；建筑（总称）」（第 2 个义项：建筑在整体上呈现的式样与构造）；句意为「她为写论文研究了这座老城的建筑」。画面里有老城街道、仰头的游客与一排石拱。

pos.zh: 名词：建筑学；建筑术；建筑风格；建筑作品；体系结构

derivatives.zh: 由同一希腊词根构成，义为「建筑师；缔造者」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「建筑的；建筑学的」
由 architectural 加 -ly 构成，义为「在建筑上」
由同一希腊词根派生，义为「建筑原理；结构学」

senses.title: The art of designing buildings
senses.definition: the art, science, and study of designing buildings and other structures
senses.definitionCN: 设计建筑及其他构筑物的艺术、科学与学问
senses.example: He went to Rome to study architecture.
senses.exampleCN: 他去罗马学习建筑学。
senses.why: Greek arkhitekton named the master builder; the abstract noun names the knowledge and craft that make him one.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 arkhitekton 命名总建造师；这个抽象名词命名的是使他成为总建造师的知识与手艺。

senses.title: The style of buildings
senses.definition: the style in which buildings are designed, especially that of a period or place
senses.definitionCN: 建筑设计所呈现的式样，尤指某一时期或地方特有的式样
senses.example: She studied the architecture of the old town for her thesis.
senses.exampleCN: 她为写论文研究了这座老城的建筑。
senses.why: What the craft produces can be seen in stone: the style of a town is its architecture made visible.
senses.whyCN: 手艺的产物能在石头里被看见：一座城的风格就是变得可见的建筑学。

senses.title: The structure of a system
senses.definition: the overall structure and organization of a computer system, organization, or other complex thing
senses.definitionCN: 计算机系统、组织或其他复杂事物的整体结构与编排方式
senses.example: The architecture of the network must be redrawn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网络的体系结构必须重新绘制。
senses.why: Any complex thing has load-bearing parts and a plan, so the building word moves to systems.
senses.whyCN: 任何复杂事物都有承重部件与一张图，于是建筑词转向系统。

senses.title: Buildings taken as a body of work
senses.definition: buildings and other structures considered together, especially those of a place or period
senses.definitionCN: 被整体看待的建筑物，尤指某地或某时期的建筑
senses.example: The city's architecture mixes glass towers and stone courts.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的建筑混合了玻璃高塔与石砌庭院。
senses.why: The built things are still called by the name of the art that made them.
senses.whyCN: 被建造出来的众多事物，仍用造就它们的这门艺术之名来称呼。

intro.en: Architecture is the abstract noun of architect, and it gathers the whole craft under one name.
intro.cn: architecture 是 architect 的抽象名词，把整套手艺收在一个名字之下。

items.en: Arkhitekton, 'chief builder', joins arkhi- 'chief' with tekton 'builder'.
items.cn: arkhitekton「总建造师」把 arkhi-「首要的」与 tekton「建造者」连在一起。

items.en: Latin forms architectura, the craft and knowledge of the master builder.
items.cn: 拉丁语造出 architectura，指总建造师的技艺与知识。

items.en: French architecture passes the noun into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 architecture 在十六世纪把这个名词带入英语。

items.en: The word first names the art, then the style that the art leaves in stone.
items.cn: 这个词先命名这门艺术，随后命名这门艺术留在石头上的风格。

items.en: The word extends to systems and organizations, where structure also carries weight.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到系统与组织，因为那里的结构同样要承重。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the architect family; the near-meaning group gathers words for buildings, structure and style.
note.cn: 形近组收 architect 的词族；近义组收表示建筑、结构与风格的词。

entries.definition: The person who designs buildings or systems.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的来源词，义为「建筑师；缔造者」。

entries.definition: Relating to architecture.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「建筑的、建筑学的」。

entries.definition: In architectural terms.
The main beam resting on columns.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「额枋」，古典建筑中横在柱子上的主梁。

entries.definition: A structure with walls and a roof.
entries.definitionCN: 有墙有顶的建筑物，比 architecture 更具体。

entries.definition: The way parts are arranged and joined together.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分被安排与连接的方式，对应 architecture 的体系结构义。

entries.definition: A characteristic manner of design.
entries.definitionCN: 设计上特有的方式，对应 architecture 的风格义。

entries.definition: The plan or arrangement of something before it is made.
entries.definitionCN: 事物被造出之前的方案与安排，是 architecture 的核心动作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the craft to the stone, then to the system.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从手艺走到石头，再走到系统。

normal.en: Architect plus -ure: the craft of the chief builder.
normal.cn: architect 加 -ure：总建造师的手艺。

normal.en: The craft leaves a style in stone: that is architecture.
normal.cn: 手艺在石头上留下风格，那就是建筑。

normal.en: A computer network also has a plan and load-bearing parts.
normal.cn: 计算机网络也有图纸与承重部件。

normal.en: The buildings of a city are its architecture in the plural.
normal.cn: 一座城的建筑群，就是复数的建筑艺术。

normal.en: Architecture is what remains after the builders leave.
normal.cn: 建造者离开之后留下的东西，就是建筑。

abstract.en: Craft, style and structure are one word at three distances.
abstract.cn: 手艺、风格与结构，是同一个词在三种距离上。

abstract.en: The word makes a whole city into a single work.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一整座城变成一件作品。

abstract.en: Order is its true subject.
abstract.cn: 秩序才是它真正的主题。

examples.en: He went to Rome to study architecture.

examples.en: She studied the architecture of the old town for her thesis.
examples.cn: 她为写论文研究了这座老城的建筑。

examples.en: The architecture of the network must be redrawn.
examples.cn: 这个网络的体系结构必须重新绘制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿奇泰克切尔」——总建造师的图纸铺满桌面，石头照着它排开：建筑学

root: architecture 是 architect 的抽象名词，来自拉丁语 architectura，源头是希腊语 arkhitekton「总建造师」，由 arkhi-「首要的」与 tekton「建造者」构成。这个词先命名建造的手艺，再命名手艺留在石头上的风格，进而指一整批建筑作品。现代又把它移到一切有承重部件的复杂结构上：计算机网络与组织都有自己的体系结构，也就是它们的图纸与骨架。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses run from craft to stone to system: the art itself, the style it leaves, a body of buildings, and the structure of a complex thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法从手艺走到石头再走到系统：艺术本身、它留下的风格、一批建筑作品，以及复杂事物的结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a master plan on the table, with columns, arches and rooms following one order.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的一张总图，柱子、拱与房间都按同一秩序排开。

branches.en: THE CRAFT LINE: the knowledge of designing is itself the subject.
branches.cn: 手艺线：设计的知识本身就是主题。

branches.en: THE STYLE LINE: a period leaves its manner in stone.
branches.cn: 风格线：一个时期把它的手法留在石头上。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM LINE: a network has a plan and load-bearing parts.
branches.cn: 系统线：网络有图纸，也有承重部件。

branches.en: THE CITY LINE: buildings together are one body of work.
branches.cn: 城市线：建筑合在一起，成为一批作品。

branches.en: THE ORDER LINE: craft becomes visible as style.
branches.cn: 秩序线：手艺变成看得见的风格。

intro.en: Architecture is architect plus the abstract suffix -ure, and the Greek halves remain readable.
intro.cn: architecture 是 architect 加抽象后缀 -ure，希腊语的两半仍然可辨。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is architectura, built on the borrowed Greek architectus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 architectura，建立在借来的希腊词 architectus 上。

items.meaning: the art or style of building
items.example: The architecture of the library is severe and calm.
items.exampleCN: 这座图书馆的建筑风格严峻而宁静。

items.example: The architect revised the plan twice.
items.exampleCN: 建筑师两次修改了图纸。

items.example: The town has great architectural value.
items.exampleCN: 这座小镇有很高的建筑价值。

items.example: The two halls are architecturally similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两座礼堂在建筑上相似。
他们简化了系统体系结构。

items.meaning: a place where building design is taught
items.example: He entered architecture school at twenty.
items.exampleCN: 他二十岁进入建筑学院。

items.example: The museum is a landmark of modern architecture.
items.exampleCN: 这座博物馆是现代建筑的地标。

definition_zh: 管；管子；软管；（英）地铁；显像管
definition_en: a long hollow cylinder, usually for carrying liquid or air, or the underground railway in London
core_image: 一根细长的玻璃管横在桌上，里面有一小段液体在慢慢移动
scene: 实验室的桌上放着一根弯成弧形的玻璃管，液体在里面缓缓推进。 The water runs through a narrow tube to the garden.
sceneCN: 这里 tube 是「管；管子」（第 1 个义项：用来输送液体或气体的中空长圆筒）；句意为水经过一根细管流向花园。桌上那根弧形玻璃管，就是这个词的画面。

collocations.phrase: the inner tube of a tyre

derivatives.zh: 由 tube 加 -ular 构成，义为「管状的」
与 tube 同源的词，义为「块茎」
由 tube 加 -ing 构成，义为「管材；管道系统」

senses.title: The hollow cylinder
senses.definition: a long narrow hollow object, usually round, used to carry or hold liquid, air, or paste
senses.definitionCN: 细长中空的圆形物，用来输送或盛放液体、气体、膏体
senses.example: The water runs through a narrow tube to the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 水经过一根细管流向花园。
senses.why: Latin tuba meant a straight horn, a hollow pipe used for sound, and the shape carried over to every pipe.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tuba 指直筒号，一种用于发声的空管，这个形状随后延伸到各种管子。

senses.title: The London railway
senses.definition: the underground railway system, especially in London, whose tunnels are long round tubes
senses.definitionCN: 特指伦敦的地下铁路系统，其隧道就是长长的圆筒
senses.example: She takes the tube to work every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上乘地铁上班。
senses.why: The first deep lines in London ran in circular tunnels, so passengers simply called the railway the tube.
senses.whyCN: 伦敦最早的深层线路在圆形隧道中穿行，于是乘客干脆把这套铁路叫作 the tube。

senses.title: The electronic display tube
senses.definition: the glass tube inside old televisions and radios that produced pictures or amplified signals
senses.definitionCN: 旧式电视与收音机中产生图像或放大信号的玻璃管
senses.example: The old radio still hums with warm tubes inside.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧收音机里温热的电子管还在嗡嗡作响。
senses.why: A device shaped like a pipe and doing work inside it naturally took the name of the shape.
senses.whyCN: 形如管、又在管里干活的装置，自然就取了这种形状的名字。

intro.en: Tube comes from the Latin tuba, a long straight trumpet, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: tube 来自拉丁语 tuba（长直号），经法语进入英语。

items.en: Tuba named a long straight horn, a hollow tube that carried sound.
items.cn: tuba 指长直号，即传递声音的空管。

items.en: French tube kept the shape but broadened the use to any hollow pipe.
items.cn: 法语 tube 保留形状，把用途扩展到各种空管。

items.en: English tube first named glass pipes used in science.
items.cn: 英语 tube 最初指科学用的玻璃管。

items.en: The nineteenth century applied it to the tunnels of the London underground.
items.cn: 十九世纪把它用在伦敦地铁的隧道上。

items.en: Electronics used it for the sealed glass part that lights up.
items.cn: 电子学用它指封在玻璃里会发亮的部件。

note.en: The first group shares the tube stem, the second holds other words for pipes and channels.
note.cn: 第一组共享 tube 词干，第二组收其他表示管道与通道的词。

entries.definition: Shaped like a tube.
Tube material or a set of tubes.
A thick underground stem such as a potato.
A tube for carrying water or gas.
A soft flexible tube.
A solid or hollow round shape with straight sides.

normalIntro.en: Tube is a short round word for a short round shape, and English uses it for any long hollow thing.
normalIntro.cn: tube 是个短圆的词，指的就是短圆的形状，英语用它称呼任何细长的中空之物。

normal.en: A tube of toothpaste puts the paste inside the shape.
normal.cn: a tube of toothpaste 就是把牙膏装在这个形状里。

normal.en: The adjective is tubular, not tube-like in form.
normal.cn: 形容词是 tubular，而不是 tube-like。

normal.en: In London, the tube needs a capital letter.
normal.cn: 在伦敦，the tube 常用大写。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s: tubes.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：tubes。

normal.en: The Latin source tuba also named a trumpet.
normal.cn: 拉丁语来源 tuba 也曾指一支号。

abstract.en: A thin glass line holding a small column of liquid.
abstract.cn: 一根细玻璃线上托着一小段液体。

abstract.en: A long round tunnel with lights inside.
abstract.cn: 一条里面亮着灯的圆形长隧道。

abstract.en: A paste being squeezed to the very last turn.
abstract.cn: 一管膏体被挤到最后一卷。

examples.en: Squeeze the tube gently until the glue reaches the paper.
examples.cn: 轻轻挤这管胶，直到胶流到纸上。

examples.en: We took the tube from the station to the market.
examples.cn: 我们从车站坐地铁到了市场。

examples.en: The nurse connected the tube to the bottle.
examples.cn: 护士把管子接到瓶子上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「兔卜」——兔子钻进地里的圆筒洞，正是 tube 那根管子。

root: 拉丁语 tuba（长直号）经法语 tube 进入英语，本义为空心管；同族词有 tubular、tubing、tuber。

sensesIntro.en: First the physical pipe, then the tunnels of the London railway, then the glass parts of radios and televisions.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是实物的管子，再到伦敦铁路的圆形隧道，最后是收音机与电视里的玻璃管。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curved glass tube holding liquid.
core.cn: 核心意象：盛着液体的弯玻璃管。

branches.en: The pipe branch: carrying water, air, or paste.
branches.cn: 管道分支：输送水、气或膏体。

branches.en: The railway branch: a tunnel become a line.
branches.cn: 铁路分支：隧道变成了线路。

branches.en: The electronics branch: glass doing the work.
branches.cn: 电子分支：玻璃在里面干活。

branches.en: The shape branch: all of them are hollow and round.
branches.cn: 形状分支：全都是中空而圆的。

branches.en: The inside branch: the name belongs to the space within.
branches.cn: 内部分支：这个名字属于里面的空间。

intro.en: Tube is a short Latin stem that English builds on with -ular, -ing and -er.
intro.cn: tube 是短小的拉丁词干，英语在上面加了 -ular、-ing 与 -er。

latinIntro.en: Latin tuba, a straight horn, is the direct source, and the words below share the tube shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tuba（直号）是直接来源，下面的词共享「管」的形状。

items.example: The stem names the hollow shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名中空的形状。

items.example: It completes the modern spelling of tube.
items.exampleCN: 它补成 tube 的现代拼写。

items.example: It forms tubular, like a tube.
It forms tubing, tubes as a group.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tubing，成套的管子。

items.example: The set has two glass tubes.
items.exampleCN: 这套装置有两根玻璃管。

items.example: The old horn shares the shape of the word.
items.exampleCN: 那支古号与这个词共享形状。

items.example: The root swells into a round body.

definition_zh: 广告（英式口语）；提及、谈到（advert to，正式）；使人注意
definition_en: a British informal word for an advertisement, or a formal verb meaning to refer to something or to draw attention to it
core_image: 一只手把路人的脸轻轻掰向亮着的橱窗
scene: 电影开场前那几分钟，屏幕上一连放了好几段推销短片。 She skipped every advert before the film started.
sceneCN: 这里 advert 是英式口语里的「广告」（第 1 个义项：广告）；句意为电影开场前她把每一段广告都跳过了。

pos.zh: 动词（正式）：提及；使人注意

derivatives.zh: 与本词同族的名词，由 advertise 加 -ment 构成，义为「广告」；本词正是它的缩略形式
与本词同族的动词，义为「做广告；宣传；登广告招聘」
由 advert 与 editorial 缩合而成的混成词，义为「社论式广告」

senses.title: A British word for an advertisement
senses.definition: a notice, picture, or short film that promotes a product, service, or event, used chiefly in British informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 推广商品、服务或活动的告示、图片或短片，主要用于英式口语
senses.example: He put an advert in the local paper for a second-hand bike.
senses.exampleCN: 他在本地报纸上登了一则二手自行车的广告。
senses.why: British speakers cut the long word advertisement down to its first two syllables, and the clipped form became the everyday spoken word.
senses.whyCN: 英国人把长词 advertisement 砍到开头两个音节，这个截短的形式就成了日常口语里的说法。

senses.title: To refer to something formally
senses.definition: to refer to a fact, topic, or event briefly, especially in speech or writing; used with to and mostly formal
senses.definitionCN: 简短地提到某个事实、话题或事件，尤见于讲话或文章，常与 to 连用，语体正式
senses.example: He adverted briefly to the earlier report.
senses.exampleCN: 他简短地提到了先前那份报告。
senses.why: Latin advertere is 'to turn toward', so to advert to a subject is to turn one's words in that direction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 advertere 是「使转向」，所以 advert to 某话题就是把话头转向那个方向。

senses.title: To draw attention to something
senses.definition: to call attention to something, often a risk or a detail that others have overlooked
senses.definitionCN: 使人注意到某事，常指别人忽略的风险或细节
senses.example: The report adverted to the danger of relying on one supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 报告提示了只依赖一家供应商的危险。
senses.why: Turning someone toward a thing is the physical act behind the word: first the head turns, then the attention follows.
senses.whyCN: 把某人转向某物，正是这个词背后的身体动作：头先转过去，注意力随后跟上。

intro.en: Advert has two histories in one spelling: a Latin verb about turning attention, and a nineteenth-century British clipping of advertisement.
intro.cn: advert 这同一个拼写里装着两段历史：一段是拉丁语中表示「转动注意力」的动词，一段是十九世纪英式英语对 advertisement 的截短。

items.en: Ad 'to, toward' plus vertere 'to turn' formed advertere, 'to turn toward'.
items.cn: ad「朝向」加 vertere「转」构成 advertere，意为「使转向」。

items.en: The same verb also came to mean 'to turn the mind to, notice, pay attention', and this is the sense English kept.
items.cn: 同一个动词后来也表示「把心思转向、注意到、留意」，英语保留的正是这一层意思。

items.en: French developed avertir from the Latin verb, with the sense of turning someone's attention, often as a warning. Whether English took the verb through French or straight from Latin is not fully settled.
items.cn: 法语从这一拉丁动词发展出 avertir，意思是把人的注意力转向某处，常带警告意味。英语是经法语还是直接借自拉丁语，尚无定论。

items.en: The verb advert is recorded in the fifteenth century with the senses 'to notice' and 'to mention', usually with to.
items.cn: 动词 advert 在十五世纪有记录，义为「注意到」与「提及」，通常与 to 连用。

items.en: The noun advert is a clipped form of advertisement and is now marked as British and informal; the verb survives mainly in formal writing.
items.cn: 名词 advert 是 advertisement 的截短形式，如今标为英式口语；动词则主要残存于正式书面语。

note.en: The look-alike group is the advertising family the clipped noun belongs to; the near-meaning group gathers other words for public notices and promotion.
note.cn: 形近组是这个词所属的广告词族；近义组收其他表示公开告示与推广的词。

entries.definition: The full noun for a public notice that promotes something; the word this clipping comes from.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告」，是推广某事物的公开告示，也是本词截短前的完整形式。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make a product, service, or job known to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「做广告；宣传；登广告招聘」，与名词同属一族。

entries.definition: The activity or industry of promoting goods and services.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告业、广告活动」，由 advertise 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: An advertisement written and laid out to look like an ordinary article.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「社论式广告」，由 advert 与 editorial 缩合而成。

entries.definition: A short film promoting a product, broadcast on television or radio; a noun in this use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电视或广播广告」，特指播出的一段推销短片。

entries.definition: A public statement giving information; it need not sell anything.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公告、通知」，只提供信息，不一定要推销东西。

entries.definition: A sign or printed sheet giving information or a warning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「告示、通知」，指提供信息或警告的牌子或印刷品。

entries.definition: Activity that publicizes a product, often with special offers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「推广、促销」，指宣传商品的活动，常伴随优惠。

entries.definition: An informal word for a mention that publicizes something, as on a show.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「（节目里的）宣传、推销」，属口语说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb advertere 'to turn toward' and the clipped noun's British setting.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 advertere「使转向」，以及这个截短名词的英式语境。

normal.en: Advertere is 'to turn toward': an advert turns your eyes toward a product.
normal.cn: advertere 是「使转向」：一条 advert 就是把你的眼睛转向某个商品。

normal.en: The verb keeps the older sense, so to advert to something is to turn your words toward it.
normal.cn: 动词保留更早的意思：advert to 某事就是把话头转向它。

normal.en: British speech clips advertisement to advert, just as it shortens many long borrowed words.
normal.cn: 英式口语把 advertisement 截成 advert，就像它缩短许多借来的长词一样。

normal.en: An advert break is the slot in which the turning of attention is sold.
normal.cn: advert break 就是拿「让人转头」这件事去卖钱的时段。

normal.en: Advert and avert look close but pull opposite ways: one turns toward, the other turns away.
normal.cn: advert 与 avert 长得像，方向却相反：一个转向，一个转开。

abstract.en: Picture a hand gently turning a passer-by's face toward a lit window.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻轻把路人的脸转向亮着的橱窗。

abstract.en: That single turn of the head is the whole history of the word: toward a product, toward a fact, toward a risk.
abstract.cn: 这一个转头的动作就是这个词的全部历史：转向商品、转向事实、转向风险。

abstract.en: An advert asks for a second of attention; the verb advert spends that second on a subject.
abstract.cn: 一条广告只求一秒钟的注意力；动词 advert 则把那一秒花在某个话题上。

examples.en: He put an advert in the local paper for a second-hand bike.
examples.cn: 他在本地报纸上登了一则二手自行车的广告。

examples.en: She never watches the adverts between the programmes.
examples.cn: 节目之间的广告她从来不看。

examples.en: He adverted briefly to the earlier report.
examples.cn: 他简短地提到了先前那份报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃特」——阿德把路人的头一掰，全都转向橱窗：广告。

root: 拉丁语 advertere「使转向」，由 ad-「朝向」+ vertere「转」构成；动词「提及、使人注意」由此而来，名词 advert 则是 advertisement 的截短，属英式口语。

sensesIntro.en: Only a few senses survive: the clipped British noun for an advertisement, and the formal verb for turning attention or words toward something.
sensesIntro.cn: 现代留下的义项不多：英式口语中作 advertisement 缩略的名词，以及正式语体中表示把注意力或话语转向某事的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand turns a passer-by's face toward a lit shop window.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把路人的脸转向亮着的橱窗。

branches.en: THE NOUN: a long borrowed noun is clipped into one brisk spoken word.
branches.cn: 名词线：一个长长的借词被砍成一个干脆的口语词。

branches.en: THE PLACEMENT: printed pages and broadcast slots are where that clipped noun lives.
branches.cn: 投放线：报纸版面与播出时段就是这个截短名词的活动场所。

branches.en: THE MENTION: the formal verb turns the flow of speech toward a topic.
branches.cn: 提及线：正式的动词把话语的流向转向某个话题。

branches.en: THE WARNING: attention is drawn to a risk before it does damage.
branches.cn: 提醒线：在风险造成伤害之前，把注意力引到它身上。

branches.en: THE SHARED TURN: whether selling, mentioning or warning, something is being turned toward the listener.
branches.cn: 共同转向：无论是推销、提及还是提醒，都是把某物转向听者。

intro.en: Advert rests on the Latin prefix ad- and the verb vertere; English adds ordinary endings to build the advertising family.
intro.cn: advert 建立在拉丁语前缀 ad- 与动词 vertere 之上；英语再加上普通词尾构成广告词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere and advertere are recorded; the noun advert is not a Latin form but a modern English clipping.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 与 advertere 都有记录；名词 advert 并非拉丁语形式，而是现代英语的截短。

items.example: It joins vertere to form advertere.
items.exampleCN: 它与 vertere 结合构成 advertere。

items.example: The turning root is shared with convert and reverse.
items.exampleCN: 这个表示「转」的词根与 convert、reverse 共用。

items.example: English took its formal verb from this form.
items.exampleCN: 英语的正式动词就来自这个形式。

items.meaning: an activity or an action in progress
items.meaningCN: 活动，或正在进行的动作

items.meaning: an advertisement written like an article
items.example: The magazine placed an advertorial beside the feature.
items.exampleCN: 杂志在专题报道旁放了一篇社论式广告。

derivatives.zh: 与本词同族的动词，义为「做广告；宣传；登广告招聘」
由 advertise 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「广告」
由 advertise 加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告活动」

definition_zh: 曲调；旋律；调音；调校
definition_en: a series of musical notes that is pleasant to hear, or to adjust an instrument or an engine so that it works well
core_image: 一双手拧紧琴弦上的木栓，弦音渐渐对上
scene: 屋里有人弹着旧木琴，低声哼一段熟悉的旋律。 She hummed a tune she had learned from her mother.
sceneCN: 这里 tune 是「曲调；旋律」（第 1 个义项：一串悦耳、可哼唱的乐音）；句意为她哼着一支从母亲那里学来的曲子。拧紧琴栓让音对上的那双手，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 tune 加 -er 构成，义为「调音器；调谐器」
由 tune 加 -ful 构成，义为「悦耳的」
由 tune 加 -less 构成，义为「不成调的；走调的」

senses.title: The hummed melody
senses.definition: a short series of musical notes that people can sing or remember easily
senses.definitionCN: 一段易于哼唱和记住的乐音
senses.example: She hummed a tune she had learned from her mother.
senses.exampleCN: 她哼着一支从母亲那里学来的曲子。
senses.why: In the Middle Ages a tune was simply a sound or a tone, and a string of tones became a melody.
senses.whyCN: 在中世纪，tune 只是声音或音调，一串音调便成了旋律。

senses.title: Making the note right
senses.definition: to adjust the strings or keys of an instrument so the notes are correct
senses.definitionCN: 调整乐器的弦或键，使音高正确
senses.example: He tuned the guitar before the concert began.
senses.exampleCN: 演出开始前他给吉他调了音。
senses.why: Since a tune is a tone, to tune is to bring an instrument into the right tone.
senses.whyCN: 既然 tune 是音调，那么 to tune 就是把乐器调进正确的音调。

senses.title: Fitting a machine to its best
senses.definition: to adjust an engine or a device so that it runs smoothly and efficiently
senses.definitionCN: 调整发动机或装置，使其运转顺畅高效
senses.example: The mechanic tuned the engine until it ran quietly.
senses.exampleCN: 机械师把发动机调校到运转安静为止。
senses.why: An engine also has to be brought into harmony, and the ear language travelled to machines.
senses.whyCN: 发动机也需要调到和谐状态，于是耳朵的语言走进了机器。

intro.en: Tune is a variant of tone, both from the Latin tonus, a stretched string and the sound it makes.
intro.cn: tune 是 tone 的变体，二者都来自拉丁语 tonus，指绷紧的弦以及它发出的声音。

items.en: Tonos meant a stretching, and then the pitch of a stretched string.
items.cn: tonos 意为拉紧，后指绷紧的弦的音高。

items.en: Tonus kept both the tension and the sound of a string.
items.cn: tonus 同时保留了弦的张力与声音。

items.en: French had ton for tone and tune for the sound of music.
items.cn: 法语用 ton 表示音调，用 tune 表示音乐的声音。

items.en: English tune named a sound or a mood as well as a melody.
items.cn: 中古英语 tune 既指声音、心情，也指旋律。

items.en: The verb extended from strings to engines and radios: tuned and tuned in.
items.cn: 动词从琴弦扩展到发动机与收音机：tuned 与 tuned in。

note.en: The first group shares the tune stem, the second holds other words for melody and pitch.
note.cn: 第一组共享 tune 词干，第二组收其他表示旋律与音高的词。

entries.definition: A device or person that tunes.
Pleasant to listen to.
Without a clear melody.
A series of notes that make a song.
The quality or pitch of a sound.
To change something slightly to fit better.

normalIntro.en: Tune is tone with a different vowel: a string held at the right tone makes a tune.
normalIntro.cn: tune 就是换了元音的 tone：弦定在正确的音调上，就成了曲子。

normal.en: In tune and out of tune are the two most useful phrases.
normal.cn: in tune 与 out of tune 是最有用的两个搭配。

normal.en: The past form simply adds d: tuned.
normal.cn: 过去式直接加 d：tuned。

normal.en: Tune in means listen to a station.
normal.cn: tune in 意为收听某个电台。

normal.en: The verb works for engines as well as instruments.
normal.cn: 这个动词既用于乐器也可用于发动机。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s: tunes.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：tunes。

abstract.en: A wooden peg turned a little until the string agrees.
abstract.cn: 木栓转一点，直到弦声对上。

abstract.en: Someone humming while walking, unaware of it.
abstract.cn: 一个人边走边哼，自己都没察觉。

abstract.en: Two voices meeting on the same note.
abstract.cn: 两个声音在同一个音上相遇。

examples.en: He whistled a tune from an old film as he worked.
examples.cn: 他一边干活一边吹着一支老电影里的曲子。

examples.en: The piano needs to be tuned before the concert.
examples.cn: 音乐会前钢琴需要调音。

examples.en: The team spent the summer tuning the machine.
examples.cn: 团队花了一个夏天调校这台机器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吞」——旋律好听，一听就把它整个吞下去，就是 tune 这支曲调。

root: 拉丁语 tonus（紧绷的弦与音调），经古法语 tune 进入英语，与 tone 同源；同族词有 tuner、tuneful、tuneless。

sensesIntro.en: First the melody you can hum, then the act of tuning an instrument, then the act of tuning a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是能哼出来的旋律，再是给乐器调音，最后是给机器调校。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a peg turned until the string answers.
core.cn: 核心意象：木栓转到弦声回应。

branches.en: The melody branch: notes put in a remembered order.
branches.cn: 旋律分支：按记得的顺序排好的音。

branches.en: The instrument branch: bringing strings to the right pitch.
branches.cn: 乐器分支：把弦调到正确的音高。

branches.en: The machine branch: harmony for an engine.
